title: Build cycle (#900): test the sccache opt-in and the lighter dev profile on Linux

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

body:
PR #913 (`Refs #900`) makes `cargo xtask gate` use sccache as a shared compile cache when it is on PATH, and lightens the dev profile (line-table debug info for our crates, none for dependencies, dependency `opt-level` 1). It was written and measured on Windows only; the maintainers have no Linux machine. This issue is for a contributor on Linux.

What to do, on the PR's branch (`issue/900-build-cache`) or on `main` once #913 is merged:
1. Without sccache installed: `cargo xtask gate quick --dry-run` and one real `cargo xtask gate test <any test name>` - the gate must run exactly as before (no wrapper set, no error).
2. Install sccache, then build the same test binary from an empty `target/` twice in two different checkouts or worktrees: note the cold time, the second (warm cache) time, the `sccache --show-stats` hit rate and the `target/` size. Do not export `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` as an environment variable (sccache hashes `CARGO_*` variables; on Windows that gave 0 cross-worktree hits).
3. Check the opt-outs: `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1` and a pre-set `RUSTC_WRAPPER` must both win.
4. Check a panic backtrace of a failing test still shows file:line with the new debug settings.
5. Is the C code (flecs, built through `cc`) cached on Linux? On Windows/MSVC it is not.

Report the numbers and anything that broke as a comment here (and on #913 if it is still open). A fix, if one is needed, is a small PR against `xtask/` (a process file: bump `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`).

Windows numbers for comparison are in PR #913's body.

Done means: the five points above are answered for Linux in a comment, and any breakage has a PR or its own issue.
